scenes.say: Smog season in Delhi. A family asks: how dirty is the air inside my room today, and what is the cheapest thing that cleans it?

scenes.title: Five short questions
scenes.say: Five short questions: city, room size, windows, purifier, and who lives there, which is never stored.

scenes.title: Outdoor PM2.5, now and next 24 h
scenes.say: Right now Delhi's forecast is 157 micrograms of PM2.5 outside: very poor on the CPCB scale, with the official health statement, word for word.

scenes.title: Inside the room: a range
scenes.say: Inside a small bedroom with the windows closed: 37 to 147. Closed, with a fan box running: 1 to 9. Always a range, never one number.

scenes.title: The purifier the room needs
scenes.say: The room needs up to 15 cfm of clean air for India's limit of 60, and up to 134 for the WHO guideline of 15. The US EPA tested this home-made box at about 400.

scenes.title: One tap: Hindi
scenes.say: One tap, and the whole plan is in Hindi.

scenes.title: Checked against 8 Delhi homes
lines: Kulshreshtha & Khare, Atmos. Pollut. Res. 2011: PM2.5 inside and outside 8 homes
Summer: 7 homes without an indoor source, ratio 0.71-0.97, all inside the 0.59-0.99 range
Winter: cooking fuel and incense, 1.13-5.64x outdoor: the range is a floor
scenes.say: We checked the model against PM2.5 measured in eight Delhi homes. In summer, all seven without an indoor source fell inside the windows-open range. In winter, cooking fuel and incense pushed kitchens higher, so the screen calls the range a floor. A small sample: a check, not proof.

scenes.say: Ghar Ki Hawa: free, open source, built for a cheap phone on 3G.
